explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/434: for k ≤ n, among A ⊆ {1,…,n} with gcd(A) = 1 and |A| = k, is the number of non-representable integers (sums of elements of A with repetition) maximised by {n, n−1, …, n−k+1}? (yes, Kiss). The Lean statement: for n ≥ 1 and 2 ≤ k ≤ n, the count for the interval [n−k+1, n] is the greatest element of the set of counts over admissible S. Restricting to k ≥ 2 is necessary and explained (for k = 1 the singleton {n} fails gcd 1 unless n = 1). The interval itself is admissible (k ≥ 2 consecutive integers have gcd 1), so IsGreatest is the right encoding; counts are finite because gcd = 1, and 0 is representable via the empty multiset. Faithful.
